DECK: Discipleship Experience (Section 4) Christology

Q1. In explaining Luke 24:25–27, how does the lesson define the theological term "hermeneutical framework"?
A. A systematic method of memorizing Hebrew root words to translate the Old Testament accurately.
B. A practical, step-by-step strategy for conducting effective soul-winning in urban centers.
C. A specific lens or science of Bible interpretation used to read and understand the scriptures.
D. An ancient church creed established to guard local congregations against heresies.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson defines a hermeneutical framework as a way of reading Scripture, grounded in the science of biblical interpretation.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD I — [09:27]–[10:15] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Luke 24:25–27

Q2. Why did Jesus address the two sad disciples on the road to Emmaus as "foolish ones and slow of heart" instead of offering immediate emotional comfort?
A. Because they had abandoned the apostles in Jerusalem during a time of intense political persecution.
B. Because the realm of the spirit operates on the consciousness of the Word, not on emotions
C. Because they refused to believe the eyewitness testimony of the women who had visited the empty tomb that morning.
D. Because their grief was causing them to walk away from their assigned geographic ministry destination.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents Jesus’ response as correcting the disciples’ understanding through Scripture rather than simply responding to their sadness.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD I — [03:29]–[04:31] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Luke 24:25–27

Q3. What detail does the lesson highlight to prove that John 1:1 was written as a deliberate theological commentary on Genesis 1:1?
A. Both books were originally transcribed in Aramaic during the exilic period in Babylon.
B. The Greek Septuagint translation of Genesis 1:1 and John 1:1 open with the exact same phrasing.
C. John explicitly cites Moses by name in the opening sentence of his Gospel account.
D. The original Hebrew text of John's Gospel was discovered alongside the Genesis scrolls at Qumran.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says the matching opening in the Septuagint links John’s opening to Genesis.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD I — [14:49]–[15:41] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Genesis 1:1; John 1:1

Q4. How does John 1 resolve the chronological puzzle of light appearing in Genesis 1:3 days before the physical sun and moon were created?
A. It explains that Genesis 1:3 refers to atmospheric lightning caused by rapid thermal expansion.
B. It reveals that the light was Christ Himself, whose divine life was the creative light of men.
C. It shows that Moses used metaphorical poetry rather than a literal chronological sequence.
D. It clarifies that the sun was actually created in Genesis 1:1 but was hidden by heavy vapor clouds.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies the light in Genesis 1 with Christ, referring to John 1’s description of life and light.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD I — [17:42]–[18:47] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Genesis 1:3; John 1

Q5. When Joshua encountered the man standing with a drawn sword in Joshua 5 and fell down to worship him, why was this act of worship NOT considered blasphemy?
A. Because Joshua was an anointed military commander who possessed special exemption from the Second Commandment.
B. Because the figure was a physical divine manifestation of Yahweh Himself.
C. Because Old Testament saints were permitted to worship holy angels prior to the giving of the Mosaic Law.
D. Because Joshua was actually worshipping the holy ground beneath his feet rather than the person standing before him.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson identifies the figure Joshua worshipped as a manifestation of God, not an ordinary angel.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN II — [07:21]–[08:24] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 John 4:2–3 | Added from online research: Joshua 5:13–15 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Joshua%205:13-15/)

Q6. According to Genesis 15:1–5 and 1 Samuel 3:10, how should we understand the phrase "the Word of the Lord came"?
A. As an audible voice.
B. As a poetic literary device used by ancient prophets to express human intuition.
C. As a physical, visible Divine Person.
D. As a secret message passed through angelic messengers to the high priest.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson interprets ‘the Word of the Lord came’ in these passages as a personal, visible encounter.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [10:30]–[13:11] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Genesis 15:1–5; 1 Samuel 3:10

Q7. How does the lesson explain Jesus' statement in John 8:58, "Before Abraham was, I am"?
A. Jesus was referring to His pre-ordained selection in the mind of God before creation.
B. Jesus was asserting His pre-existence, having personally interacted with Abraham in Genesis.
C. Jesus was referring to the immortal nature that all human souls possess prior to biological birth.
D. Jesus was claiming that His earthly human lineage could be traced back genealogically before Abraham.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson connects Jesus’ claim with the Word of the Lord’s earlier personal encounters with Abraham.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [13:11]–[14:14] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 Samuel 3 | Added from online research: John 8:58 (https://esv.org/verses/John+8:58)

Q8. According to the lesson, what is the primary doctrinal difference between Christ's Old Testament manifestations and His New Testament Incarnation?
A. In the Old Testament He appeared as an angel, whereas in the New Testament He appeared as a prophet.
B. In the Old Testament He assumed temporary physical forms, but in the Incarnation He was permanently born as a true man.
C. In the Old Testament He possessed limited divine power, but in the New Testament He received full omnipotence.
D. In the Old Testament He spoke only to Israel, but in the Incarnation He spoke exclusively to the Gentiles.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes temporary Old Testament manifestations from Christ’s birth as a true man in the Incarnation.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [14:14]–[15:28] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Added from online research: Isaiah 9:6 (https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Isaiah%209%3A6&version=ESV); John 1:14 (https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=John%201%3A14&version=ESV)

Q9. What makes Christ the ultimate standard when we are commanded to be "imitators of Christ"?
A. He bypassed real human emotional limitations through His divine omniscience.
B. He lived out God's character in human shoes, proving that divine righteousness is applicable to human existence.
C. He laid down His divine attributes permanently and functioned purely as a human prophet.
D. He established an easier way suited for fragile human nature compared to the Old Testament standard.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents Christ’s genuinely human, sinless life as the example believers are to imitate.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN II — [15:12]–[17:30] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 1:18

Q10. How does the revelation of God in Jesus Christ refine our understanding of God's nature under the Law?
A. It shows that the Law were not the full expression of God's nature.
B. It proves God was vengeful in the Old Testament but changed His personality in the New Testament.
C. It shows that the Law was authored by angels rather than God.
D. It proves that God's grace did not exist prior to the birth of Jesus in Bethlehem.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Jesus reveals aspects of God’s nature, such as mercy and grace, not fully expressed in the Law.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN II — [17:30]–end of transcript (approximate boundary)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 1:18

Q11. How do we resolve the contradiction between Jesus "growing in wisdom" (Luke 2:52) and Jesus being the All-Knowing God?
A. Jesus only feigned ignorance in public so His peers wouldn't feel uncomfortable.
B. He is omniscient, but in His human nature He voluntarily experienced human development.
C. His divine nature completely replaced His human mind once He turned thirty.
D. Luke 2:52 is talking about spiritual growth rather than actual cognitive development.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson explains that Jesus is all-knowing in His divine nature and experienced growth in His human nature.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN III — [02:31]–[04:54] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Luke 2:52

Q12. Why is it crucial for our redemption that Jesus suffered as a genuine human rather than a divine manifestation?
A. Because if He were only divine, the crucifixion would be acting rather than actual human suffering absorbing the penalty of sin.
B. Because angels are incapable of entering physical blood covenants.
C. Because divine beings cannot experience physical fatigue or emotional sadness.
D. Because the Mosaic Law required a human priest to offer a human sacrifice to satisfy the altar's requirements.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lessons connect Christ’s humanity with real suffering and with His ability to die for humanity’s sins.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN II — [09:49]–[12:10] and JESUS- SON OF MAN III — [16:01]–[16:56] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 John 1:7; Romans 5:11

Q13. How does the reality of hematidrosis (sweating drops of blood) substantiate the doctrine of Christ’s humanity?
A. It proves that Jesus contracted a physical disease right before His arrest.
B. It serves as proof of extreme human stress, proving He was never insulated from human pain.
C. It proves that the blood shed in Gethsemane had more redemptive power than the blood shed on the cross.
D. It demonstrates that Jesus was physically weaker than most religious martyrs.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents the blood-like sweat as evidence of the extreme stress Jesus experienced as a human.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN II — [11:00]–[12:10] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Added from online research: Luke 22:44 (https://www.esv.org/Luke+22%3A44/)

Q14. How does the lady turned "detective" illustrate the believer's duty to "love the Lord with all your mind" (Matthew 22:37)?
A. Genuine love naturally produces an intense, investigating hunger.
B. True devotion requires believers to know their faith well to win debates against secular scholars.
C. A loving heart must constantly cross-examine church leaders to verify whether their personal life matches their doctrine
D. Loving God with the mind means experiencing emotional expressions during worship.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The illustration links love for God with a desire to know more about Him.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [02:38]–[04:30] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Matthew 22:37

Q15. Why does Apostle state that Christianity and Buddhism are fundamentally incompatible ("we cannot both be right")?
A. Buddhism denies the existence of moral evil, whereas Christianity teaches that evil is inherited from Adam.
B. Buddhism teaches that world miseries end when we do what is right, whereas Christianity teaches we must believe what is right to be empowered to do what is right.
C. Buddhism claims spiritual enlightenment is achieved through suffering, while Christianity claims suffering is always a sign of demonic influence.
D. Buddhism rejects the reality of an afterlife, whereas Christianity teaches that we live eternally in heaven or hell.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The Apostle contrasts the two teachings about what ends the world’s miseries and how people are enabled to do what is right.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [07:41]–[08:41] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Hebrews 1:6

Q16. Which scripture directly dismantles the Jehovah's Witness assertion that Jesus is merely the archangel Michael?
A. John 11
B. Hebrews 1
C. Matthew 28
D. Colossians 2
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson cites Hebrews 1 to show Jesus receives worship and does works associated with God, rather than being merely an angel.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [08:41]–[09:36] and [13:34]–[14:58] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Hebrews 1:6; Hebrews 1:3 | Also cited in lesson segment: John 1:3; Mark 2; John 5:22; Revelation 19:16; Revelation 11; Daniel 7

Q17. What combination of divine Deeds ("D") and Seat ("S") in the HANDS acronym belongs exclusively to Jesus?
A. Creating the universe, forgiving sins, exercising final judgment, and occupying God's eternal throne.
B. Parting waters, giving divine commandments, defeating earthly armies, and ruling over angels.
C. Establishing the Church, indwelling believers, authoring Scripture, and interceding for saints.
D. Raising the dead, instituting communion, abolishing the Old Covenant, and establishing physical Israel.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson gives creation, forgiveness of sins, final judgment, and God’s throne as evidence of Christ’s deity.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [12:24]–[14:58] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: John 1:1; Revelation 1:8; Isaiah 9:6; John 8:58; John 20:28; John 1:3; Mark 2; Hebrews 1:3; John 5:22; Revelation 19:16; Revelation 11; Daniel 7

Q18. Why did the Sanhedrin condemn Jesus for blasphemy when He claimed the title "Son of Man" before Caiaphas?
A. Because "Son of Man" was a political title reserved for the earthly King of Israel.
B. Because He was invoking Daniel 7.
C. Because the title implied that God had entered human existence through biological reproduction.
D. Because claims of divine sonship were strictly forbidden under the traditional oral rabbinic code.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lessons connect Jesus’ words before the high priest with Daniel 7 and explain that His hearers understood the claim as one to deity.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [14:58]–[15:57] and JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [23:41]–[25:26] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Daniel 7 | Also cited in lesson segment: Mark 2; Hebrews 1:3; John 5:22; Revelation 19:16; Revelation 11; Isaiah 9:6; Mark 14

Q19. How does the lesson explain the Old Testament concept of the "Two Yahwehs"?
A. As a metaphor describing the dual nature of God's justice and God's mercy.
B. As an invisible Yahweh in heaven and a physical Yahweh who appeared visibly as a man on Earth.
C. As an early Hebrew misunderstanding that was later corrected by the New Testament writers.
D. As a reference to the distinction between Yahweh the Creator and the Angel of Death.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson describes a Yahweh in heaven and another Yahweh manifesting visibly on earth.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [08:24]–[10:30] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Genesis 15

Q20. According to Hebrews 2:10–14, what does it mean that Christ is the Archegos (Captain/Fountainhead) of our salvation?
A. He sits safely in heaven sharing instructions on how we should live.
B. He paved the way through death and legally brought us into adoption as His brethren.
C. He replaced angels as the chief military officer over physical earth wars.
D. He serves as a legal advocate only for those who observe Levitical priesthood laws.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Christ entered into suffering and death to bring believers into salvation and adoption as His brethren.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN III — [15:06]–[16:56] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Hebrews 2:10–14 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 5:11

Q21. Why is the fulfillment of Psalm 22:16 ("They pierced my hands and my feet") powerful proof of divine prophecy?
A. Because King David studied ancient execution methods used by foreign nations.
B. Because when David wrote that prophecy, the execution method known as crucifixion did not even exist yet.
C. Because Jesus gave the Roman soldiers written instructions on how to fulfill the prophecy.
D. Because it is the only verse in the Old Testament that describes physical pain.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Psalm 22 described pierced hands and feet centuries before crucifixion existed.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN III — [08:42]–[09:39] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Psalm 22:16 | Also cited in lesson segment: Philippians 3

Q22. According to 1 John 4:2–3, what is the ultimate litmus test for discerning whether a spiritual teacher is of God?
A. Their ability to work undeniable physical miracles.
B. Their confession affirming Jesus Christ both in His full humanity and deity.
C. Their public commitment to living an ascetic lifestyle free from worldly riches.
D. Their alignment with historical church hierarchies and ordained leadership.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents confession of Christ’s coming in the flesh as a test and emphasizes His humanity as well as His deity.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN II — [06:41]–[08:57] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: 1 John 4:2–3 | Also cited in lesson segment: 2 John 1:7

Q23. What is the theological significance of distinguishing between "a child is born" and "a son is given" in Isaiah 9:6?
A. "Child is born" refers to His earthly ministry; "Son is given" refers to after resurrection.
B. "Child is born" points to the beginning of His humanity, while "Son is given" reveals His pre-existent Sonship.
C. "Child is born" applies to Israel's national birth; "Son is given" refers to the spiritual adoption of believers.
D. "Child is born" signifies His flesh; "Son is given" signifies the Holy Spirit coming upon Him at baptism.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lessons contrast the beginning of Jesus’ humanity with His eternal Sonship.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [16:58]–[18:00] and JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [15:28]–[16:34] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Isaiah 9:6 | Also cited in lesson segment: Daniel 7

Q24. What forms the true foundation of a Christian’s bold confidence before the throne of grace?
A. God looking at us through the lens of who we are in Christ and what Christ has legally accomplished for us.
B. The believer’s personal record of flawless obedience and religious commitment.
C. The emotional feelings of warmth experienced during church services.
D. The public praise given to a believer by spiritual leaders.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson grounds confidence before the throne of grace in being reckoned in Christ and in what Christ has done.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN III — [18:50]–[19:59] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 5:12; Romans 5:17

Q25. Why do all human beings inherit a fallen nature because of Adam's sin?
A. Every human being signed a spiritual contract in heaven agreeing to Adam's choice.
B. Inheritance of sin is governed by demonic assignments rather than covenant representation.
C. Death was introduced as an penalty rather than a structural legal reality.
D. Adam was God's covenant representative for all humanity.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Adam represented humanity and that his sin affected those who came after him.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN III — [11:57]–[12:52] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Genesis 5:2

Q26. Based on Genesis 5:2, what vital detail is revealed about the word "Adam"?
A. "Adam" is not merely one man's proper name, but the Hebrew word for mankind.
B. "Adam" was a royal title given exclusively to Abraham’s spiritual lineage.
C. "Adam" translates directly to "sinful flesh" in ancient Egyptian texts.
D. The name "Adam" was invented by Moses.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says ‘Adam’ refers to mankind, not only to one individual.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN III — [10:52]–[12:52] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Genesis 5:2

Q27. What vital lesson does the pastor draw from the historic confrontation between Athanasius and Arius at Nicaea?
A. Theological disagreements are personal power struggles that fractured early church unity.
B. The defense of precise biblical doctrine by individuals preserved the true understanding of Christ's Deity for future generations.
C. Church doctrine are more authoritative than Scripture when settling arguments about the Trinity.
D. Early church fathers relied on alliances rather than Scripture to establish doctrine.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson credits Athanasius’s defense of Christ’s deity with helping preserve a clear understanding of Scripture.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN II — [04:47]–[06:41] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 John 4:2–3

Q28. Why is Jesus called both a "Child [that] is born" and "The Everlasting Father" within the single prophecy of Isaiah 9:6?
A. Because Jesus transforms into God the Father whenever He ascends into the heavenly sanctuary.
B. Because while His humanity had an origin in time, His divine identity as God is eternal, without beginning or end.
C. Because Isaiah was combining two separate prophecies written by different authors into one text.
D. Because "Everlasting Father" was a title.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lessons contrast the beginning of Jesus’ humanity with His eternal divine identity.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [16:58]–[18:00] and JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [15:28]–[16:34] (approximate ranges)

Q29. What combination of actions directed toward Jesus under the "H" in the HANDS acronym proves His Deity?
A. Performing public miracles, receiving tithes, and appointing twelve apostles.
B. Receiving direct worship, hearing prayers, and having saving faith placed explicitly in Him
C. Calming the storm, rebuking religious hypocrites, and forgiving executioners on the cross.
D. Reading human thoughts, fasting forty days, and promising physical thrones to His followers.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson cites worship, prayer, and faith placed in Jesus as evidence of His deity.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [08:41]–[09:36] (approximate range)

Q30. Using the lesson's practical illustration of a phone call vs. a video call, what defines a "mediated encounter" with God in the Old Testament?
A. Communicating through a distinct physical medium or manifestation, such as a burning bush or pillar of fire.
B. Reading written prophecies inscribed on stone tablets through an ordained Levitical priest.
C. Experiencing emotional conviction during high moments of congregational worship and sacrifice.
D. Seeking guidance through casting physical lots like the Urim and Thummim.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson defines a mediated encounter as communication through a medium, with the burning bush and pillar of fire as examples.

Q31. What does the speaker say loving God with all one's mind includes?
A. Limiting devotion to attending church and singing songs.
B. Focusing only on receiving blessings, healing, and breakthroughs.
C. Avoiding difficult sermons and books that require rereading.
D. Deliberately investing effort in learning more about Jesus, including through books and repeated study.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker connects loving God with the mind to becoming interested in knowing Jesus and putting one's mind to that task.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [03:32; 04:30]

Q32. How does the speaker use the relationship analogy of becoming a 'detective' to describe love for God?
A. A believer should investigate church leaders' private lives before worshipping.
B. A Christian should gather facts only to win debates against other religions.
C. Genuine commitment includes a desire to know more about the one loved, rather than receiving benefits without interest in the person.
D. A person should expect God to provide gifts before learning about him.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker says someone in love wants to learn details about the other person and applies this to seeking to know the Lord, not merely receiving benefits.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [02:38; 03:32]

Q33. Why does the speaker emphasize Jesus' question, 'Who do you say that I, the Son of Man, am?'
A. Because Jesus was asking only whether his disciples knew his preferred title.
B. Because what people say about Jesus matters, and believers should know and be able to explain who he is.
C. Because the question was intended to establish that Jesus was only a prophet.
D. Because the disciples' opinions mattered more than what Scripture says.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says Jesus cares what people say about him and contrasts Christian teaching with other accounts of Jesus.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [05:26]

Q34. Which contrast does the speaker draw between Christian claims about Jesus and the examples he gives of other religions' views?
A. He says Muslims call Jesus a prophet, Jehovah's Witnesses a great angel, and Hindus say he has been reincarnated many times; he contrasts these with Christianity's claims about Jesus.
B. He says Muslims teach repeated reincarnations, Jehovah's Witnesses call Jesus a great teacher, and Christians call him only a prophet.
C. He says all these groups agree that Jesus is the eternal Son of God and fully divine.
D. He says each group differs only over whether Jesus performed miracles.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker lists Muslims' view of Jesus as a prophet, the Jehovah's Witness view of him as a great angel, and Hindu claims of repeated reincarnations, then contrasts these with Christian teaching.

Q35. How does the speaker contrast Buddhism's account of suffering with the Christian account he presents?
A. He says Buddhism teaches salvation through faith in Jesus, while Christianity teaches repeated reincarnations.
B. He says Buddhism teaches that the world's miseries end when people do what is right, while Christianity teaches that people must believe what is right to be empowered to do what is right.
C. He says both accounts teach that suffering ends only through physical discipline.
D. He says Christianity teaches that people can do what is right without first believing what is right.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker contrasts the Buddhist claim about doing what is right with his stated Christian claim about believing what is right and being empowered to do it.

Q36. In the speaker's HANDS acronym for defending Christ's deity, what do the letters represent?
A. Humanity, Atonement, New birth, Discipleship, and Salvation.
B. Holiness, Authority, Nature, Death, and Sonship.
C. Honor, Attributes, Deeds, and Seat.
D. Heaven, Angels, Names, Dominion, and Scripture.

Q37. Which example does the speaker use under 'Honor' as evidence for Jesus' deity?
A. Jesus refuses worship from the Magi and redirects it to the angels.
B. The Father commands the angels to worship Jesus, and the Magi also worship him as a toddler.
C. The angels worship Jesus only after he takes his seat at the final judgment.
D. The Magi honor Jesus as a king but the speaker says they do not worship him.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker cites Hebrews 1:6 and the Magi's worship of the child Jesus as examples of honor belonging to God.

Q38. Which set of qualities does the speaker place under the 'Attributes' part of HANDS?
A. Hunger, fatigue, sleep, and growth in wisdom.
B. Eternity, almightiness, and divine names such as 'Mighty God' and 'Alpha and Omega.'
C. The ability to teach parables and choose twelve disciples.
D. The ordinary virtues of generosity, patience, and courage.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker calls eternity and almightiness incommunicable attributes and points to divine titles in John 1:1, Revelation 1:8, Isaiah 9:6, and John 8:58.
REF: JESUS- SON OF MAN I — [11:04]

Q39. Which group of actions does the speaker cite under 'Deeds' as actions of Jesus that belong to God?
A. Building the temple, leading Israel out of Egypt, and writing the law on stone.
B. Creating all things, forgiving sins, sustaining all things, and exercising final judgment.
C. Choosing twelve apostles, instituting communion, and appointing church elders.
D. Healing the sick, teaching crowds, and travelling through Galilee only.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker cites John 1:3, Mark 2, Hebrews 1:3, and John 5:22 when describing divine deeds attributed to Jesus.

Q40. What does the speaker mean by the 'Seat' in the HANDS acronym?

EXPLANATION: The speaker distinguishes seeing God face-to-face through a medium from seeing God's face, which he says no one can do and live.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [04:24]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: John 1:18 | Also cited in lesson segment: Genesis 1; Exodus 33:11

Q84. What example does the speaker use to clarify a mediated 'face-to-face' encounter?
A. A person reading a letter without knowing who wrote it.
B. A phone or video call, where people speak face-to-face through a medium without literally seeing each other's face in person.
C. A person meeting another in a room but refusing to look at them.
D. A dream in which the speaker says no words are exchanged.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker compares mediated encounters with switching from a phone call to a video call, while still communicating through a medium.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [05:24]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Exodus 33:11

Q85. What distinction does the speaker draw between the Word's Old Testament appearances and the incarnation?
A. The Word was a human man throughout the Old Testament and became an angel at the incarnation.
B. The Word appeared only as an audible voice before becoming a physical object after the incarnation.
C. The Word appeared in forms such as a flame, the angel of the Lord, or a human figure, but was not a man until he was born as a human in the incarnation.
D. The speaker says the Word had no Old Testament appearances and first appeared at the resurrection.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker lists Old Testament manifestations including a burning bush, the angel of the Lord, and a visible human form, then distinguishes these from becoming flesh and being born as a proper man.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [06:21; 14:14]

Q86. How does the speaker describe the visitor who met Abraham while the other two visitors went to Sodom?
A. He says one of the three was Yahweh, while the other two were angels who went to Sodom.
B. He says all three were ordinary human travelers and none was identified as God.
C. He says two were Yahweh and one was an angel who stayed in Sodom.
D. He says the visitor was Samuel and the other two were prophets.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says one of the three visitors was Yahweh and the two others were angels who went into Sodom.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [09:23]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Genesis 18:1–3; 19:1

Q87. What wording in Abraham's conversation does the speaker use to illustrate two Yahwehs?
A. Abraham says he will send fire from two angels who remained in Sodom.
B. The two angels tell Abraham that Yahweh has no authority over Sodom.
C. Abraham says that the Lord will send rain from the stars.
D. The Yahweh speaking with Abraham says he will rain fire from Yahweh on high.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker points to the statement that Yahweh will rain fire from Yahweh on high as an example of one Yahweh speaking about another.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [09:23]

Q88. What does the speaker argue about the Old Testament phrase 'the Word of the Lord came' in the accounts of Abraham and Samuel?
A. He says the phrase always meant an audible sound with no visible encounter.
B. He says it refers only to a prophet's private interpretation of events.
C. He presents the Word of the Lord as a person encountered, noting that the Lord came and stood by Samuel.
D. He says the phrase was used only after the incarnation.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker points to Genesis 15 and 1 Samuel 3:10, emphasizing the Word of the Lord as an encountered person and that the Lord came and stood.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [10:30; 12:15; 13:11]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Genesis 15; 1 Samuel 3:10

Q89. How does the speaker connect Jesus' words 'Before Abraham was, I am' with the Word of the Lord in earlier biblical accounts?
A. He says Jesus meant that he had personally known and interacted with Abraham before Abraham existed in Jesus' earthly lifetime.
B. He says Jesus was speaking only about a future role assigned to him by God.
C. He says the phrase means Abraham was older than Jesus in every sense.
D. He says Jesus was quoting Samuel and denying that he had met Abraham.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says Jesus was not speaking metaphorically and identifies him with the Word of the Lord who appeared to Abraham.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD II — [13:11]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 1 Samuel 3

Q90. What interpretive caution does the speaker give about phrases such as 'Son of God,' 'firstborn,' and 'begotten Son'?
A. Their meaning must be understood from biblical usage and context, not assumed from a modern or literal-sounding phrase.
B. They always mean that God physically gave birth to Jesus.
C. They have one identical meaning in every biblical passage.
D. They should be interpreted only by modern Western usage.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says biblical terms must be understood in context and warns against assuming that sonship means God physically gave birth to Jesus.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [08:43; 09:46; 10:54]

Q91. What kind of sonship does the speaker say God appointed for Solomon in 1 Chronicles 28:6?
A. A sonship beginning from Solomon's virgin birth.
B. An eternal sonship that made Solomon equal with God.
C. A royal sonship associated with being chosen to build God's house and rule as David's heir.
D. A sonship meaning that Solomon was the only Israelite called God's child.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker distinguishes Solomon's general identity as a Jew from the royal sonship associated with his appointment and throne.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [11:54]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: 1 Chronicles 28:6

Q92. According to the speaker, why is Jesus called the Son of God in relation to his virgin birth?
A. No human man was involved in his conception, so the speaker relates this sonship to his birth from a virgin.
B. He says Mary was not involved in Jesus' birth.
C. He says the title refers only to Jesus' resurrection and not his birth.
D. He says the title means Jesus was adopted by Joseph after his birth.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker cites the angel's explanation that the Holy Spirit would overshadow Mary and says no human male was responsible for Jesus' procreation.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [14:37]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Luke 1; Luke 3

Q93. What example from Luke's genealogy does the speaker use when explaining the phrase 'son of God' in relation to origin?
A. Solomon is called the son of God because he was born of a virgin.
B. David is called the son of God because he built the temple.
C. Samuel is called the son of God because he was raised in the temple.
D. Adam is called the son of God even though he had no human father.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker points to Luke's genealogy ending with Adam, who is identified as the son of God, and relates that to having no human father.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [14:37]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Luke 1; Luke 3

Q94. What two conditions does the speaker associate with royal sonship in the line of David?
A. Being a prophet and building the temple in Jerusalem.
B. Belonging to David's lineage and ascending to the throne.
C. Being born in Bethlehem and serving as a priest.
D. Being the firstborn son and defeating the Philistines.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says royal sonship requires being an heir from David's line and ascending the throne.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [16:34]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Luke 1:30

Q95. How does the speaker explain the declaration that Jesus was 'Son of God' by the resurrection?
A. In the royal-sonship sense, Jesus' resurrection and enthronement fulfill the promise of David's heir reigning without end.
B. It means Jesus first became God's Son in the moment of his virgin conception.
C. It means Jesus stopped being the Son after his resurrection.
D. It means the resurrection changed Jesus from human to angel.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker connects Romans 1:4 and Hebrews 1 with Jesus' resurrection and the fulfillment of the Davidic throne promise.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [18:35]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 1:4; Hebrews 1

Q96. What does the speaker mean by calling Jesus the Eternal Son?
A. Jesus became the Son only after the Council of Nicaea.
B. Jesus was created as the first angel before becoming human.
C. Jesus became the Son only when he ascended to David's throne.
D. Jesus did not begin to be the Son at the incarnation; he has eternally existed as Son and is described as eternally generated from the Father.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says Jesus has always been the Son, eternally existing and eternally generated from the Father, rather than becoming Son at the incarnation.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [19:21]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 1:4; Hebrews 1

Q97. Why does the speaker argue that evidence for Christ's deity should also be shown from the Old Testament?
A. Because the speaker says the New Testament contains no references to Jesus' deity.
B. Because the Old Testament was written after the Gospels.
C. Because only the Old Testament can describe the Son as divine.
D. To answer claims that the doctrine arose only at Nicaea or that later New Testament writings about Jesus were altered.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker raises claims about Nicaea and alleged alteration of John and says the Old Testament appearances of the Word provide evidence.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [20:28]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Proverbs 30

Q98. What question does Proverbs 30:4 pose that the speaker highlights in support of the Son's existence?
A. After describing God's acts in creation, it asks, 'What is his name, and what is his Son's name, if you know?'
B. It says the Son's name is hidden and cannot be asked.
C. It identifies Solomon as the one who gathered the wind and established the earth.
D. It says the Son was created after the earth was established.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker highlights Proverbs 30:4's questions about who controls creation and what is his Son's name.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [21:27]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Proverbs 30:4 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 10

Q99. What happens after the Son of Man comes before the Ancient of Days in Daniel 7:9–14, according to the speaker?
A. The Son of Man is the only figure in the vision and receives no kingdom.
B. The Ancient of Days gives the Son of Man a temporary earthly throne that is later destroyed.
C. There are thrones in the vision; the Son of Man comes to the Ancient of Days and receives everlasting dominion and a kingdom served by all peoples.
D. The vision describes two angels sharing a throne and ruling only Israel.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker highlights the plural thrones, the Ancient of Days, and the Son of Man receiving dominion and an everlasting kingdom.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [22:15]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Daniel 7:9–14 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 10

Q100. Why does the speaker say Jesus' answer before the high priest was understood as a claim to deity?
A. Jesus denied being the Messiah and asked the high priest to release him.
B. Jesus said they would see the Son of Man coming in the clouds, invoking Daniel 7; the high priest reacted by tearing his clothes.
C. Jesus cited Proverbs 30:4 to claim he was Solomon's descendant only.
D. Jesus called himself a prophet, which the high priest considered a political crime.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says Jesus' words in Mark 14:62 invoked Daniel 7 and were understood by the high priest as a divine claim.
REF: JESUS- SON OF GOD III — [23:41; 25:26]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Daniel 7; Mark 14:62
